Hi Redwood team,

I just finished the Developer Quickstart guide linked from the docs and tried the hosted API example. We're a small infra team at Applify building a plugin that will make heavy inference calls, and I'm interested in a short technical demo focused on latency and cost controls.

A few quick details:
- Use case: real-time document processing (avg request length ~1k tokens)
- Primary concerns: 99th-percentile latency, batching behavior, and cache strategies
- Current infra: GCP (us-west1), Kubernetes-based, looking at both hosted and dedicated options

Can someone from the engineering or demo team run through: performance profiles, common config patterns, and a quick estimation for monthly unit costs for ~20M tokens/month?

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Ross
Senior Platform Engineer, Applify

- Tue Mar 9, 10:30–11:00 AM

3) Expected concurrency / qps target
4) Any compliance constraints (VPC, data residency)

Hi Hannah — thanks for the quick reply. Tue Mar 9, 3:00–3:30 PM PT works best for me.

Answers to your prep questions:
1) Model family: open Llama/generic quantized weights (we're evaluating multiple variants)
2) Seq length p50/p90: 256 / 1024
3) Target concurrency: ~25 concurrent requests during peak (p95 bursty)
4) Compliance: no strict residency needs, but we prefer using VPC mode for customer data

If Jasmine can dive into KV cache patterns and kernel tradeoffs that would be ideal.

See you Tue at 3 PT — please send calendar invite.

— Evan
